# Standard verbs

A noun that declares props and a store is a thing noun: it gets the standard verbs with no handler of its own. Every thing noun has each core verb; where the row's kind does not fit the store, or the store lacks what the row needs, the verb is listed but unavailable, with the reason. A verb that is not core exists on a noun only where the store has what it needs. A verb the noun declares by hand under a standard name replaces the generated one. A host mounting a tool's catalog gets the same verbs, forwarded.

| Verb | Core | Kinds | Needs | Subject | Many | Repeat | History | Undo | Confirm | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `get` | yes | collection, singleton, instances | Store.Get | yes |  |  | fetch |  |  | Read a thing's props: every prop as an object, one prop's value (prop), or some props (props) |
| `list` | yes | collection, instances | Store.List |  |  |  | fetch |  |  | List the things, each its props with id and label; where keeps the things whose props equal the values given; filter applies a named saved prop filter |
| `create` | yes | collection | Store.Create, a prop create writes |  |  |  | change | delete |  | Create a thing from the props given (each omitted one its default); answers the new thing |
| `set` (`patch`) | yes | collection, singleton, instances | Store.Patch, a writable prop | yes | yes | yes | change | restore |  | Write a thing's props: one prop (prop and value, or toggle on a boolean), or several (changes, or prop=value words); answers the thing after the write |
| `delete` | yes | collection | Store.Delete | yes | yes |  | change | recreate | `Delete {{noun}} {{label}}?` | Delete a thing (asks first) |
| `archive` | yes | collection | Store.Patch, a writable archive prop (role archive) | yes | yes | yes | change | restore |  | Archive a thing: set its archive prop |
| `edit` | yes | collection, singleton, instances | Store.Get, Store.Patch, a writable prop, forms.edit | yes |  |  | action |  |  | Edit a thing's writable props in a form; supplied props write directly without opening a form |
| `watch` |  | collection, singleton, instances | Store.Watch, else Store.List (a singleton: Store.Get) | yes |  |  | fetch |  |  | Stream what happens to the things (one, or those where matches): a JSON line per thing added, modified or deleted, from since when given; the CLI streams until interrupted |
| `rename` |  | collection, singleton | Store.Patch, a writable label prop (role label) | yes |  | yes | change | restore |  | Rename a thing: write its label prop (name; to when the key prop is named name); the form opens on the old name |
| `move` |  | collection | Store.Patch, a writable owner prop (role owner) | yes | yes | yes | change | restore |  | Move a thing to another owner: write its owner reference (to) |
| `duplicate` |  | collection | Store.Get, Store.Create, a prop create writes | yes | yes |  | change | delete |  | Create a copy of a thing: every prop create writes, from the thing, with prop=value overrides (pairs or changes); answers the new thing |
| `restore` |  | collection | Store.Patch, a writable archive prop (role archive) | yes | yes | yes | change | restore |  | Restore an archived thing: clear its archive prop |

The subject is the parameter named after the noun's key prop: given, it names the thing; left out, it is the thing the request acts for (the focus). Many runs once over a visual selection, as one undo step; a verb without both a subject and many is never run over a selection. Undo says how history.undo reverts the change: delete the thing made, restore the props written, or recreate the thing removed. Repeat: `.` repeats the write when it writes only simple values (enum, boolean, number, duration).

## Nouns with props

<a id="noun-ochazuke.page"></a>
### `ochazuke.page`

Store kind `instances`. Standard verbs: `archive` (unavailable: its store is a instances; archive is for a collection), `create` (unavailable: its store is a instances; create is for a collection), `delete` (unavailable: its store is a instances; delete is for a collection), `edit`, `get`, `list`, `set` (`hide`, `patch`, `show`), `watch`. Its own verbs: `next`, `open`, `pick`, `previous`.

| Prop | Type | Flags | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | key |  | The page id |
| `title` | string | read-only, role label |  | The page's title (its tab) |
| `hidden` | boolean |  |  | Out of the tabs and ctrl+j/k (the pages.hidden setting); page.open still opens it |
| `active` | boolean | read-only |  | The current page |

<a id="noun-ochazuke.setting"></a>
### `ochazuke.setting`

Store kind `collection`. Standard verbs: `archive` (unavailable: its store writes no props (no Store.Patch)), `create` (unavailable: its store creates no things (no Store.Create)), `delete` (unavailable: its store deletes no things (no Store.Delete)), `get`, `list`, `watch`. Its own verbs: `add`, `append`, `cycle`, `decrease`, `edit`, `increase`, `multiply`, `prepend`, `remove`, `reset`, `revert`, `set`, `show`, `toggle`, `write` (`save`).

| Prop | Type | Flags | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | key |  | The setting's name |
| `type` | string: string, integer, number, boolean, duration, list | read-only |  | The value's type |
| `default` | string | read-only |  | The default value, in its file form (a duration as 400ms) |
| `value` | string | read-only |  | The value in effect, in its file form: the session's, else settings.json's, else the default (setting.set writes it) |
| `enum` | list | read-only |  | The values allowed, when the setting limits them |
| `protected` | boolean | read-only |  | Only the owner may change this setting, even with the agent rights gate off |
| `description` | string | read-only |  | What the setting does |
| `section` | string | read-only |  | The section of its owner it is filed under (Setting.Section, else the name before its first dot, else general; settings.sections lists them) |
| `owner` | string | read-only |  | The owner it is filed under, a tab of the Settings page: app (the application's), ochazuke (the framework's, also when the application changed its default) or one the application declares (settings.owners lists them) |
| `group` | string | read-only |  | The heading it sits under inside its section, when it has one |
| `origin` | string: default, file, session | read-only |  | Where the value in effect comes from: the default, settings.json or this session (setting.show --verbose says more) |
